CausalChain: Chronic liver injury -> early HCC development -> secretion of tumor-derived exosomes -> emergence of a distinct exosomal microRNA profile (e.g., miR-21, miR-221) -> concomitant release of ctDNA with tumor-specific methylation alterations (e.g., RASSF1A, GSTP1) -> integration via advanced bioinformatics and digital molecular assays -> combined biomarker signature detectable before radiologic changes -> correlation with aggressive tumor features
Hypothesis: In patients with chronic liver disease, integrating tumor-derived exosomal miRNA signatures—including miR-21 and miR-221—with specific ctDNA methylation alterations from key tumor suppressor genes such as RASSF1A and GSTP1 will serve as an early, sensitive, and robust biomarker panel for aggressive hepatocellular carcinoma detection, including in AFP-negative cases. Leveraging advanced digital droplet PCR, next-generation sequencing technologies, and machine learning-enabled bioinformatics pipelines, this integrative approach can detect composite molecular signatures before conventional radiologic manifestations and correlate these profiles with aggressive tumor behavior.
Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer mortality, particularly in patients with chronic liver injury where early detection is crucial. In this study, we propose that an integrated liquid biopsy approach—combining tumor-derived exosomal microRNA (miRNA) profiles, including established candidates such as miR-21 and miR-221, with ctDNA methylation patterns affecting tumor suppressor genes (e.g., RASSF1A, GSTP1)—can serve as an early, sensitive biomarker panel for aggressive HCC. Using state-of-the-art techniques such as digital droplet PCR, next-generation sequencing, and advanced machine learning algorithms for data integration, we aim to detect a combined biomarker signature prior to radiologic changes. This approach is particularly targeted toward patients with chronic liver disease, including those with AFP-negative HCC, and seeks to correlate molecular alterations with aggressive tumor phenotypes.
Orignal_vs_New: The revised hypothesis retains the original concept of integrating exosomal miRNAs with ctDNA methylation to detect aggressive HCC but enhances specificity and practical implementability. It now explicitly identifies candidate miRNAs (miR-21, miR-221) and ctDNA methylation markers (RASSF1A, GSTP1), incorporates contemporary technologies such as digital droplet PCR and next-generation sequencing, and outlines the use of machine learning for bioinformatics integration. These modifications refine each step of the original causal chain—linking chronic liver injury to early HCC development, exosomal miRNA secretion, ctDNA methylation alterations, and the emergence of a combined signature detectable prior to radiologic changes, with a direct correlation to tumor aggressiveness.
